title: Nungbi (Luireishimphung) Black Stone Pottery Settlement
title_translation: Ancestral Craft Cradle of Wheel-less Serpentinite Pottery
creator: Nungbi Pottery Custodians & Archaeological Survey
publisher: Documented in Horam 1977, Roy 1961, Manipur Cultural Directorate
notes: Historic northern settlement celebrated globally for its ancient craft of hand-shaped black stone pottery (Hampai), fashioned without a potter's wheel from a sacred blend of weathered serpentinite stone and weathered clay.
indigenous_tangkhul_chronicle: Nungbi (Luireishimphung) village-hi northern Ukhrul-li wheel-less black stone pottery (Hampai)-wui ancestral cradle kashung akha.
Serpentinite stone kala weathered black clay ngarum-da artisans-na manual sculpting-li unique cookware sakya.
Megalithic lungchei monoliths kala pottery rituals ancestral craftsman thot-li reverence shitsangya.
english_translation_text: Nungbi (Luireishimphung) in northern Ukhrul is the world-renowned ancestral home of wheel-less black stone pottery (Hampai).
Artisans blend crushed serpentinite rock with weathered alluvial clay, shaping vessels entirely by hand without a potter's wheel.
The settlement preserves ancient commemorative megaliths (Lungchei) and seasonal taboos honoring craft ancestor spirits.
chronicle_milestones: 1. Ancient Era: Discovered by northern Tangkhul pioneers finding unique serpentinite stone outcrops along the river gorge.
2. Craft Evolution: Perfection of the wheel-less shaping technique, polishing with mountain bamboo and river stones.
3. 19th Century: Nungbi cooking pots traded across Manipur, Nagaland, and the Kabaw Valley for iron, salt, and silk.
4. Contemporary: Global recognition and Geographical Indication (GI) registration candidacy for indigenous cultural preservation.
geographical_scope: Nungbi Khullen & Nungbi Kajui, Northern Ukhrul (Elevation 1,550 m)
historical_significance: One of the rarest living Neolithic ceramic traditions in Asia, proving centuries of indigenous mineral engineering and artistic refinement.

historical_terms.Hampai: Traditional wheel-less black stone pottery vessel
historical_terms.Kachikang: Hand burnishing and shaping of clay vessels
